memo.recommendation_rationale: We recommend a PASS on BrightPath Dental Partners due to a critical dealbreaker failure in customer concentration, where single-customer revenue reaches 34.6% [p.11] (Sunshine Health) against our maximum 20% [p.11] threshold. The transaction presents additional high-severity risks, including top-five customer concentration of 80.1% [p.11], earnings adjustments accounting for 30.8% [p.3] of adjusted EBITDA, key-person disruption from the planned post-close departure of VP of Operations Dana Whitfield [p.13], and payor contracts allowing 90-day [p.11] terminations. Consequently, the asking price of $12.1M [p.18] representing a 9.0x [p.18] adjusted EBITDA multiple is unsupportable.
memo.business_overview: BrightPath Dental Partners is a dental support organization (DSO) founded in 2013 [p.3] and headquartered in Tampa, Florida [p.3] that operates 11 [p.3] affiliated practices across central Florida [p.3] with 88 [p.6] employees. The company generates revenue by providing centralized management, administrative, revenue cycle, marketing, and procurement services to its affiliated practices under management agreements. While 7 [p.4] acquisitions have been completed to date, the deal materials omit practice-level clinical, financial, and geographic performance details across the 11 [p.3] locations. Furthermore, detailed extracted fields regarding company description, end markets, service lines, revenue model, top customers, and management composition remain pending review.
memo.financial_summary:
BrightPath Dental Partners reported revenue of $6.8M [p.3] in 2022, $8.1M [p.3] in 2023, and $9.3M [p.9] in 2024, representing a headline compound annual growth rate of 16.9% [p.4]. However, this growth incorporates 7 [p.4] completed acquisitions, and organic same-store performance is not disclosed. Gross profit progressed from $2.3M [p.3] in 2022 to $2.7M [p.3] in 2023 and $3.0M [p.3] in 2024. Working capital indicators demonstrate steady deterioration, as days sales outstanding increased from 52.0 [p.10] in 2022 to 55.5 [p.10] in 2023 and 58.1 [p.10] in 2024. Additionally, management's narrative attributing revenue weighting to Q4 benefit resets is contradicted by historical quarterly results where Q4 revenue ($1.7M [p.10] in 2022, $2.0M [p.10] in 2023, and $2.3M [p.10] in 2024) consistently lagged Q2 and Q3 revenue ($1.8M [p.10] in 2022, $2.1M [p.10] in 2023, and $2.4M [p.10] in 2024).

Earnings quality exhibits significant divergence between reported and adjusted EBITDA: reported EBITDA was $0.8M [p.3] in 2022, $0.9M [p.3] in 2023, and $0.9M [p.3] in 2024, compared to adjusted EBITDA of $1.0M [p.3] in 2022, $1.2M [p.3] in 2023, and $1.3M [p.3] in 2024. Adjusted EBITDA margins were 14.7% [p.3] in 2022, 14.8% [p.3] in 2023, and 14.0% [p.3] in 2024. Total add-backs of $0.40M [p.3] account for 30.8% [p.3] of 2024 [p.3] adjusted EBITDA, exceeding prudent limits and diluting earnings quality, while specific add-back line items remain pending review.
memo.thesis_commentary: BrightPath Dental Partners achieves an overall thesis score of 32% [p.3] with 100% [p.3] criterion coverage under the services rollup strategy. The company meets thesis standards in baseline revenue scale ($9.3M [p.9] actual vs. $5M–$50M [p.9] target), EBITDA margin floor (14.0% [p.3] actual vs. >=12% [p.3] target), and top-line growth (16.9% [p.4] actual vs. >=5% [p.4] target). However, it fails six key criteria, led by a dealbreaker in single-customer concentration where Sunshine Health represents 34.6% [p.11] of revenue against the <=20% [p.11] ceiling. Top-five concentration also fails at 80.1% [p.11] versus the <=50% [p.11] limit. Contracted recurring revenue reaches only 31.0% [p.3] against the >=40% [p.3] requirement, and earnings quality fails as add-backs comprise 30.8% [p.3] of adjusted EBITDA compared to the <=20% [p.3] threshold. Finally, valuation and human capital criteria fail due to an entry multiple of 9.0x [p.18] adjusted EBITDA against the <=8.0x [p.18] cap, and a failure in management continuity caused by the planned post-transaction departure of VP of Operations Dana Whitfield [p.13].

red_flags.title: Unilateral Payor Fee Revisions and 90-Day Termination Provisions
red_flags.detail: Payor contracts permit termination on short notice (90 days) and grant payors unilateral discretion to revise fee schedules, exposing the business to severe revenue loss and margin compression without contractual protection.
